summary: MiniVectorDB (question 600081), C++17, no third-party storage or vector index library. This material records the student's own prompts and the unedited output of 26 verification runs. Student contributions: (1) predicted distance arithmetic dominated query cost, with a SIMD instruction estimate; the ablation refuted it at 24%. (2) chose to pursue both the record-access and fsync optimisations against the agent's advice to stop optimising. (3) explained the 0.37 MiB I/O saving as second-file block amplification rather than payload bytes; confirmed at 3973 bytes per commit versus a 4096-byte block, then transferred to multi-table transactions (4628 vs 13353 bytes per commit). Agent-authored analysis is labelled role=agent and is not student evidence. Dimensions still lacking student evidence are marked explicitly rather than filled with agent text.

我觉得这个判断对，你继续做吧
我觉得是A 距离计算：1.28M 次浮点减乘加。用 SSE2（4 float/指令）约 32 万条 SIMD 指令
我认为可以A和B同时推进A 继续抠查询那剩下的 0.2 ms（记录访问）——收益上限约 1.5×，但查询权重 2/3 B 把写入的 2 次 fsync 合成 1 次（把提交标记写进同一个记录文件）——写入可能快近 2×，但权重只有 1/3
省下的不是 commits.log 那点内容，是"第二个文件"这件事本身的块级代价：文件系统按块/页写，每个文件都要单独分配块、写元数据、走一遍落盘路径；两次 fsync 覆盖两个文件，就是两份块对齐放大和元数据写。合并成一个文件一次 fsync，提交标记搭记录文件的同一批块和同一次落盘走，第二份文件的块级写放大和元数据开销就没了，所以 I/O 降了 0.37 MiB。

我觉得最难的约束是"崩溃后不能部分生效"和"数据超内存还要精确 TopK"这两条的组合，但真正卡人的是前者。因为超内存 + 精确 TopK 是一个静态的算法/数据结构问题，可以离线想清楚；而"崩溃后不能部分生效"是对每一条写入路径的全局不变量——它不允许你把原子性当成一个局部优化，任何一次提速（比如 B 的合并 fsync、A 的索引替换）都必须重新证明这条不变量还成立。我的判断是：这道题的设计意图不是比谁单点快，而是比谁在"改性能"和"保住崩溃语义"之间做取舍时，证据链完整。所以我把"崩溃 6/6 仍全过"当成每次改动的准入条件，而不是最后补的回归项。

我猜写入那 0.653 s 里 fsync 本身占大头。下一步做：把单次 fsync 换成 fdatasync（提交标记和记录已在同一文件、同一批块，不需要 inode 元数据持久化），预测 write T 从 0.653 s 降到 0.50 s 左右（±0.05），I/O 不变或略降，崩溃 6/6 仍须全过。如果降不到，说明瓶颈不在 fsync 的元数据部分而在块落盘本身，那我就转去测批量提交合并。

同意，"批量合并"在官方口径下不可行——提交点由测试驱动，合并多个 COMMIT 就违反"响应发出前必须完成持久化"。我修正假设为：预分配文件 + fdatasync——文件大小不再增长，fdatasync 省掉每次提交的 size/inode 元数据刷写，只刷数据块。预测 write T 从 0.602 s 降到 0.56 ± 0.03 s，I/O 基本不变（5.6 MiB 量级），崩溃 6/6 仍须全过（并注明：这仍只证明恢复逻辑，不证明持久性，SIGKILL 测不出 fdatasync 与 fsync 的差异）。证伪分支：若落在 [0.53, 0.59] 噪声带内，说明主成本是每次提交的块分配/块数而非元数据，下一步转去测"减少每次提交的块数"——把提交标记和记录头对齐到同一块，预测再降 0.02–0.03 s。

dimension_coverage.问题理解与自主拆解: student identifies crash-atomicity as a global invariant over every write path, not a local optimisation, and makes crash 6/6 a per-change admission gate (/user_prompts/7/content)
dimension_coverage.技术理解与迁移: student explanation of block amplification plus multi-table transfer (E24/E25)
dimension_coverage.实验与反馈迭代: student designs the fdatasync experiment with a quantitative prediction (0.50 +/- 0.05 s), an I/O prediction, a hard crash constraint and an explicit falsification branch (/user_prompts/8/content)
dimension_coverage.取舍与反思: student decision to pursue A+B against the agent's recommendation (E24)

retrospective.what_was_hard: The public suite only exercises normal shutdown, so it cannot see crash-path defects. Two serious defects (stale tail-block cache, transaction-id reuse after a crash) were invisible to it and were only found by a self-written SIGKILL suite.
retrospective.what_did_not_work: Assuming per-row heap allocations dominated the query cost: measuring it showed no change (E12). Assuming the memory-bounded design implied acceptable performance: it was correct but 1916 ms/query (E8).
retrospective.measurement_discipline: Every performance claim is a wall-clock number from tests/bench.py or tests/big_table_test.py on the same generated data, with answers checked against double-precision brute-force truth. After E28 showed a 6% run-to-run spread and an optimistic 0.367 ms outlier, claims use the median of three runs, matching the official three-round rule.
student_contributions: Predicted that distance arithmetic dominated the query cost, with a quantitative SIMD instruction estimate; the ablation refuted it (E19).
Chose to pursue both the record-access and fsync optimisations against the agent's recommendation to stop optimising (E24).
Explained the I/O saving as second-file block amplification and metadata rather than payload bytes; confirmed quantitatively at 3973 bytes per commit versus a 4096-byte block (E24).

limitations: ann search mode currently executes the exact path, so Recall@10 is 1.0 but no approximate index is exercised.
The record file has no compaction, so it grows with updates.
The official baseline values, resource limits and hidden cases are not published, so the local benchmark optimises absolute T/B/M rather than the published efficiency ratio.
Local M is process peak RSS; the official metric also counts page cache, so local M is a lower bound.
The platform did not expose per-item T/B/M, a failure category, or Recall for the performance run, so the reason the performance entry did not reach the board is not yet determined.
